claims.text: Near-equiatomic PtPdCoCuNi HEA nanoparticles can be prepared by a one-step colloid-based route and supported on SiO2.
The PtPdCoCuNi nanoparticles are uniformly dispersed on the SiO2 support.
The initial PtPdCoCuNi nanoparticles are a well-mixed, homogeneous, single-phase solid solution.
Pt and Pd form isolated catalytically active sites in PtPdCoCuNi/SiO2.
Mild oxygen exposure selectively oxidizes surface Co, Cu, and Ni in PtPdCoCuNi nanoparticles to form sub-nanometric oxide patches.
An oxygen partial pressure of approximately 10^-3 atm is mild enough to form beneficial oxide patches without overoxidation.
The non-noble-metal oxide patches act as physical barriers that reduce surface atomic diffusion.
Reduced surface diffusion caused by the oxide patches inhibits nanoparticle sintering.
The oxide patches prevent thermally driven phase segregation and atomic rearrangement.
Pt and Pd remain largely unoxidized when the less noble elements undergo sacrificial oxidation.
The oxide patches protect Pt and Pd sites and thereby preserve catalytic activity.
In an inert atmosphere, the absence of passivating oxide patches permits greater atomic diffusion and structural degradation.
Mildly oxidized nanoparticles will retain a homogeneous single-phase alloy structure better than the inert control.
Mildly oxidized nanoparticles will exhibit less sintering than the inert control.
Mildly oxidized nanoparticles will exhibit less compositional inhomogeneity than the inert control.
Mildly oxidized nanoparticles will maintain superior catalytic performance relative to the inert control.
Mildly oxidized nanoparticles will maintain superior thermal transport properties relative to the inert control.
The proposed oxide-passivation mechanism is effective across 773–1173 K for catalysis and 473–1923 K for thermoelectric service.
Higher oxygen partial pressure causes overoxidation, whereas lower oxygen partial pressure provides insufficient passivation.
Changing the support or elemental composition can alter the proposed stability mechanism and outcomes.

contradictions.description: The mediator requires formation of compositionally distinct surface oxide patches, while the predicted outcome unqualifiedly describes the nanoparticles as homogeneous, single-phase, and minimally compositionally inhomogeneous. These can coexist only if 'single-phase' and 'homogeneous' are explicitly restricted to the residual alloy core.

The boundary conditions predict that elevated oxygen pressure may cause overoxidation and performance loss, but the falsification rule treats degradation caused by overoxidation as refuting the mechanism. Failure outside the proposed oxygen-pressure window is consistent with the boundary rather than a decisive falsification.
